To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cutting force, tool wear and production inaccuracies (i.e., overcut and cylindricities error) are all functions of the ultrasonic power, feedrate, spindle speed, diameter and the interaction between them.

(i) the ultrasonic power and tool diameter are the most significant factors that affect the cutting force and tool wear; (ii) the spindle speed is the most significant factor that affects the overcut error and cylindricities; and (iii) the optimal machining conditions are 0.5 kW, 0.05 mm/rev, 100 rpm, and 0.8 mm, respectively, for the ultrasonic power, feedrate, spindle speed, tool diameter.

the cutting force is a function of the ultrasonic power, spindle speed, tool diameter, and feed rate; the tool wear is a function of ultrasonic power, tool diameter, spindle speed, feed rate, and the overcut error; the overcut error is a function of spindle speed, feedrate, and the tool wear; and the cylindricity errors are a function of spindle speeds, feed rate, tool diameter, ultrasonic power, and tool wear.

the optimal machining conditions for drilling high precision holes in Ti6AlV alloys are 1000 W ultrasonic power, 0.02 mm/rev feed rate, 200 rpm spindle speed, and 1.6 mm tool diameter.

the optimal machining conditions are spindle speed 1000 rpm, ultrasonic power 1000 W, feed rate 50 mm/min, and tool diameter 0.5 mm, which yield a cutting force of 0.3 kN, a tool wear of 1.5 μm, an overcut error of 0.05 mm, and a cylindricity of 0.01 mm.

the optimal machining conditions for drilling high precision holes in the workpiece made from Ti6Al4 V alloys are 100 W of ultrasonic power, 0.1 mm/s of feed rate, 2000 r/min of spindle speed, and 2.5 mm in tool diameter.
